lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Show 2,040 as standard expanded form and as tens only (how many tens?).

FEEDBACK
2,000+40; 204 tens (because 2,040÷10=204).

WATCH FOR
Non-standard partitions are wrong only if they do not equal the original number.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
For 3,060; 1,405; 2,700 write (a) standard expanded form (b) one non-standard partition (c) a short proof they are equal using regrouping.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Standard: 1,320 = 1,000 + 300 + 20. Non-standard: 1,320 = 13 hundreds + 2 tens, because 13 hundreds = 1,300.

TRY FIRST
Show 2,040 as standard expanded form and as tens only (how many tens?).

FEEDBACK
2,000+40; 204 tens (because 2,040÷10=204).
teach_steps.explain:
Numbers can be partitioned in standard place form and in non-standard ways that still equal the same total after regrouping.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Non-standard partitions are wrong only if they do not equal the original number. Correct the value or method, not just the appearance of the digits.
